title: Audio briefing production

description.need: An approved script is not a listenable briefing, and the assembly in between is what stops briefings shipping on a rhythm. Done by hand it is slow. Done carelessly it renders without an error and still ships with a clipped last word, one host audibly quieter than the other, and gaps long enough that a listener checks whether the file has stopped.
description.input: An approved multi segment script with its host turns, a target runtime, the speaking pace the adopter's listeners are used to, and any intro or bed material they supply.
description.core_action: Synthesize each turn as speech, trim the padding the synthesizer leaves at both ends before inserting the pacing that was actually intended, level the whole track once, and verify segment by segment that what was spoken is what the script said rather than trusting that a render which completed produced a finished briefing.
description.output: One finished audio file at a normal listening loudness with even levels across hosts and beds, a runtime checked against what the script promised, and a written record of which segments were synthesized, which were not, and what settings produced them.

activities.label: Read the approved script, its segment structure and its promised runtime
Settle voice per host role, speaking pace and gap length against what has been approved before
Synthesize each segment separately, uncompressed, at the settled voice and pace
Trim each segment's own padding, join with the intended gap, and level the whole track once
Check each segment against the words it was meant to speak, then the track against the promised runtime
Hand over the finished file with the settings that produced it and any segment that failed

outcomes.statement: The delivered file is finished rather than merely rendered.
success_criteria: Every segment is checked against the words it was meant to speak, not only the whole track against a target runtime.
A truncated, silent or missing segment is named in the delivery instead of being absorbed into a track that still plays end to end.
Levels are even enough across hosts, intro and bed that no listener reaches for the volume control mid briefing.

outcomes.statement: The next briefing starts from the settled production decisions instead of re-deriving them from the last file.
success_criteria: The voice held by each host role, the speaking pace and the gap length are written where the next run reads them.
A run that changed one of them records which one and why.
A first run states that it is establishing these settings rather than reporting them as unchanged.

guidance: Loudness is one number worth fixing on and then leaving alone, because every platform re-normalizes at playback anyway. What normalization will never rescue is one host quieter than the other inside the same file, since the whole track moves by a single gain. Trim each segment's own leading and trailing silence before adding pacing, or the padding compounds into dead air. A total runtime check is weak: a swallowed final syllable costs under a second and passes every tolerance. Check each segment against the words it owed.
use_cases: A small team that approved three scripts this month and shipped one, because the only person who can assemble the audio is also the person who wrote it and has a day job.
A recurring internal briefing whose whole value is arriving on the same morning every week, where a run that silently drops a segment is worse than a run that visibly did not happen.
A two host format whose voices come from different synthesis settings, so every episode arrives with one host noticeably quieter and somebody balances it by hand before publishing.
An operator being asked why the last three episodes ran eleven minutes when the show is advertised as seven, who cannot answer because nothing recorded what pace the script was written for.
A briefing moving from one destination to several, where a file mastered loud for the first one is turned down by all of them and the uneven balance inside it survives untouched.

recommended_trigger.rationale: The work has one honest starting point, a person approving a script. Nothing here is worth doing on a clock, and nothing can be done before the approval exists. A briefing that publishes on a schedule gets that schedule from the approval that precedes it, not from this step.

personalization_needs: Which voice belongs to which host role for this adopter, because the pairing is a taste decision the recipe cannot guess and it has to hold across every future briefing or the show changes character without anyone deciding to.

The speaking pace their listeners are used to, since that is what turns a word count into an expected duration and makes the per segment check mean anything. Comfortable narration sits between roughly 130 and 160 words a minute; below about 120 a listener disengages and above about 180 they tire.
How much gap the adopter wants between turns, measured after the synthesizer's own padding is trimmed rather than as raw inserted silence, because the two differ by more than the setting itself.
Whether a finished file is delivered as a file, into a folder, or into a publishing queue, because that decides what done means and where the record of the run has to land.
dependencies: ffmpeg, built with the ebur128 loudness filter and an encoder for the adopter's delivery format

input_schema.name: segment_silence_ms
input_schema.description: Gap between segments, measured after each segment's own leading and trailing padding has been trimmed rather than as raw silence added to whatever the synthesizer returned.

input_schema.name: target_lufs
input_schema.description: Integrated loudness the finished track is levelled to before delivery. Spoken word convention is around -16 LUFS with a true peak below -1 dBTP; the exact value matters far less than applying it once to the whole track.

input_schema.name: intro_audio
input_schema.description: Optional intro material the adopter supplies, joined before the briefing and levelled with the speech rather than separately. Where it lives is a binding decided at adoption, not part of the recipe.
